thread.title: Silicon Valley stocks: VMWare plunges, Maxim soars on M&A reports

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Silicon Valley stocks: VMWare plunges, Maxim soars on M&A reports
text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Jan 29, 2018, 1:34pm PST Updated Jan 29, 2018, 2:11pm PST Shares of Palo Alto-based VMWare plunged 16.57 percent on Monday on a report that it may do a reverse merger with Dell Technologies . Dell is the larger of the two companies and owns a majority stake in VMWare (NYSE: VMW). The new report, by CNBC on Monday , is speculative and follows reporting last week that suggested the opposite — Dell buying the rest of the VMWare it doesn't already own — was in the works. Meanwhile, Maxim Integrated Products (NASDAQ: MXIM) jumped 12.3 percent after a CNBC report said the Japanese chipmaker Renesas Electronics is in talks to buy the San Jose company in a deal that could be worth up to $20 billion. The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Technology Index of 13 of the largest tech stocks in the region dropped 1.33 percent on Monday, dragged down by Applied Materials, Symantec Corp . (NASDAQ: SYMC), Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) and its biggest member, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL). Shares of the Cupertino giant slid on reports that it had cut iPhone X production drastically on lackluster demand . Among all Silicon Valley stocks, the ones that saw their share prices drop the most today: • GoPro (NASDAQ: GPRO) fell 5.84 percent ahead of its upcoming earnings report , indicating that investors are fretting that there's more bad news to come out of the San Mateo-based action camera maker. Earlier this month, rumors swirled that the company had hired investment bankers to explore a possible sale. At the same time, GoPro said it was exiting the drone business and laying off hundreds of employees. • Lam Research Corp. (NASDAQ: LRCX) dipped 3.26 percent. • Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) fell 3.13 percent. • SVB Financial Group (NASDAQ: SIVB) declined 2.94 percent. The parent company of Silicon Valley Bank reported earnings last week . Along with Maxim, the other top performers among Silicon Valley stocks on Monday: • Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) jumped 3.64 percent. • Fair Isaac Corp. (NASDAQ: FICO) gained 3.57 percent. • Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) rose 2.86 percent. • Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) closed up 2.73 percent. Ranked by Local employee headcount Rank
